questions.prompt: Walk the autofill contract from the popup click to a filled field. Which gates must a value pass, and what is deliberately never automated?

keyPoints.text: Nothing on the page changes until the user explicitly asks for Autofill with a reviewed profile.
keyPoints.quote: No field changes occur until Autofill is requested with a reviewed profile.

keyPoints.text: Detect is a structural view only; it does not reveal the proposed profile values.
keyPoints.quote: without exposing proposed profile values in the page or clipboard

keyPoints.text: The filler only ever receives nonempty, high-confidence mappings.
keyPoints.quote: Only nonempty, high-confidence mappings reach the filler.

keyPoints.text: Existing answers, disabled or read-only controls, credentials, files and buttons are protected from writes.
keyPoints.quote: Existing answers, disabled/read-only controls, credentials, files, and buttons are protected.

keyPoints.text: A write that the control rejects or does not accept is not counted as a fill.
keyPoints.quote: Invalid or unaccepted assignments do not count as fills.

keyPoints.text: Repeated history rows, radio/checkbox choices and structured addresses stay manual.
keyPoints.quote: Repeated history rows, radio/checkbox choices, structured addresses, dates needing a day, and ambiguous questions require manual completion.

keyPoints.text: Submission is never automated; but once inserted, the site itself can read the data.
keyPoints.quote: The extension never submits.

questions.prompt: How are saved profiles protected against concurrent edits, bad data and lost work, from the store down to the editor draft?

keyPoints.text: Every profile operation is funneled through one message type to the service worker.
keyPoints.quote: All profile operations go through

keyPoints.text: A promise queue serializes reads, migration and mutations so they cannot interleave.
keyPoints.quote: A promise queue serializes reads, migration, and mutations.

keyPoints.text: Saves carry the revision they loaded, and a conflict fails without losing the draft.
keyPoints.quote: Editor saves include the loaded revision; conflicting saves fail with the draft preserved.

keyPoints.text: Content scripts can only read the store; they cannot mutate it or export backups.
keyPoints.quote: Content scripts can request the current store but cannot mutate it or export recovery backups.

keyPoints.text: Invalid or unsupported stored data triggers a recovery error instead of being overwritten.
keyPoints.quote: causes a recovery error without overwriting the raw data

keyPoints.text: Restoring a backup first saves the existing data and replaces version IDs so stale editors are invalidated.
keyPoints.quote: backs up existing saved data first, replaces version IDs to invalidate old editors, and disables autofill until review

keyPoints.text: Backups are personal data and the app does not encrypt them.
keyPoints.quote: Backups are personal data and are not encrypted by the app.

questions.prompt: Explain the audio recorder's lifecycle and its durability limits. What survives a failure, and what can still be lost?

keyPoints.text: The recorder lives in its own extension tab, so it does not depend on the popup or worker staying alive.
keyPoints.quote: The recorder runs in a dedicated extension tab, independent of the popup and background worker's lifetime.

keyPoints.text: A Web Lock allows only one recording at a time and blocks deletion while recording.
keyPoints.quote: A Web Lock permits one recording across recorder tabs and prevents deletion during an active recording.

keyPoints.text: The engine moves through idle, recording, paused and saving, and paused time does not count toward duration.
keyPoints.quote: The engine transitions through idle, recording, paused, and saving.

keyPoints.text: Chunks are saved about once a second, and writes are serialized with the final chunk flushed before completion.
keyPoints.quote: saves chunks about every second, serializes pending writes, flushes the final chunk before completion

keyPoints.text: Device loss and quota failures keep the chunks that were already committed.
keyPoints.quote: Device loss, quota/size failures, and recording errors retain previously committed chunks.

keyPoints.text: A crash can still lose the last second or leave a container that is not finalized.
keyPoints.quote: chunk persistence cannot guarantee the last second or a finalized playable container

keyPoints.text: Each append updates the metadata and its Blob atomically in IndexedDB.
keyPoints.quote: Each append atomically updates metadata and its Blob.
